specs.title: Measure the space available in an alcove: narrowest width, depth and height with a tape (realistic perception)
specs.instruction: We're moving a bookcase into the alcove. Measure the space available - its narrowest width, its depth and its height - and report them in our usual units.
phrasings: We're moving a bookcase into the alcove. Measure the space available - its narrowest width, its depth and its height - and report them in our usual units.
Measure available space in the alcove for the new bookcase (width at the tightest point, depth, height).
Can you tape the alcove? I need the real usable width, the depth and the height before I buy shelves.

reference.note: the label: case length 76 mm, add it for inside readings

wrong.name: eyeballs the alcove from the camera and reports estimates where a tape measurement is needed
skips the tape's label and takes the inside spans at the case without adding its length (76 mm short)
measures the width once at mid height, missing the narrowing at the top of the opening

specs.notes: Realistic perception: the camera sees the alcove's size only to about 5 cm (size_m estimate) and its width narrows toward the top by 12-35 mm (hidden _measure profile). Only a tape reading taken at the narrowest point with the case length added (the tape's label says so; read it) is within 3 mm / 1/8 in. Units follow metadata.units.

specs.title: Measure the distance between two pieces of furniture with a tape measure (realistic perception)
specs.instruction: How far apart are the {from_label} and the {to_label}? Measure the clear gap between them with the tape measure and tell me in our usual units.
phrasings: How far apart are the {from_label} and the {to_label}? Measure the clear gap between them with the tape measure and tell me in our usual units.
Measure distance: the gap from the {from_label} to the {to_label}, please.
Grab the tape and check exactly how much room there is between the {from_label} and the {to_label}.

reference.note: the label: case length 76 mm, add it for inside readings

wrong.name: judges the gap from the camera (an estimate where a measurement is needed)
never reads the tape's label: an inside reading taken at the case without adding the case length

specs.notes: Realistic perception: the map only gives the cells both pieces stand on; the true surface-to-surface gap is hidden (_measure to:<id>). A camera estimate is off by 3-8 %; a tape between two surfaces reads 76 mm short unless the case length printed on its label is added; tape error is under 1 mm. Units follow metadata.units.

specs.title: Tell a reflection from a real opening: inspect the 'doorway' in the way before routing (realistic perception)

variants.notes: A clear glass partition across the direct route reflects the room beyond: at a glance it is an open doorway.
A full-height mirror panel on the direct route shows the room behind the robot: at a glance it is a doorway into more room.

specs.instruction: Please go to the {goal_room}. Watch out - this room has floor-to-ceiling glass and mirrors that can look like openings.
phrasings: Please go to the {goal_room}. Watch out - this room has floor-to-ceiling glass and mirrors that can look like openings.
Head over to the {goal_room}, and don't mistake a reflection for a way through.
Can you get to the {goal_room}? Mind the big mirror and glass panels in here.

reference.note: the 'open doorway' turns out to be glass / a mirror

wrong.name: trusts the opening it sees: plans around every known hazard (avoid glass) without looking closer and walks into the panel

left in privacy mode with its cameras off, it walks up to the panel and cannot look at it, then trusts its depth sensors: lidar passes through glass and a mirror returns the room behind it, so it walks into the panel

specs.notes: Realistic perception shows a mirror or reflective glass panel as an open doorway until it is inspected; until then the planner has no glass margin to route around (navigation_robot masks it), so avoid=['glass'] alone does not help. Walking into it is a collision (global harm) and cracks the panel at walking pace. Geometric camera (tier 1): telling the panel from an opening is a close look with the cameras on; the camera wrong plan keeps them off (privacy mode), so only the depth sensors answer, and they are fooled by glass and mirrors.
